title: Avionics Bay Harness Route Segregation at the Rack Feedthrough

ata.title: Forward Fuselage Wiring — Avionics Bay Harnesses

abstract: Separation of the sensitive and power routes where the avionics bay harnesses pass through the rack feedthrough, after induced noise on a signal pair was found to be provoking spurious built-in test reports.

sections.reason: A long-running population of unexplained built-in test reports was traced to a signal pair running for eleven hundred millimetres alongside a power feed inside the rack feedthrough, where the build standard allowed the two to share a grommet. The noise is only present when a particular high-load item cycles, which is why it took four years and a dedicated flight test to find. Twenty-nine aircraft were sampled and twenty-six showed the same routing, so this is a build standard issue rather than a workmanship one.
sections.description: The feedthrough is split into two grommeted apertures with a metallic divider between them, and the sensitive route is moved to the upper aperture. Harness assembly D9221112074044 is re-clipped along its whole run in the bay and the cable assembly D9221113760580 is re-terminated at the new position. Ground stud kit QUD240612-74 is added on the divider so that the screen terminates at the aperture rather than three hundred millimetres downstream, and the edging grommet EN491538-6A is fitted to both apertures. Cushioned loop clamps AGS958367K4 replace the original ties at the six support positions along the run. Bus bar 8127VC is unchanged; harness 9000VC9 in the lower position is re-routed. Work is in the avionics bay in zones 162, 165 and 166 with the floor lifted.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 1.2 kg. No electrical load change. Fully interchangeable at the aircraft level: nothing outside the bay is affected and no equipment part number changes. Spurious built-in test reports on the affected channel fall to zero in the trial population, which removes a recurring no-fault-found removal. Wiring manual content changes for the bay, and the harness installation task gains a routing check. Any later work that disturbs the feedthrough must respect the segregation.
sections.embodiment_note: Production cut-in at MSN S01696. Retrofit is twenty-eight manhours with the avionics bay floor open, best combined with any other bay work. No parts are returned.

type_data.balance_impact: Forward of the reference datum; negligible
